headline: CANADA'S FIRST LARGE-SCALE URANIUM MINE IN 20 YEARS BREAKS GROUND — DENISON'S PHOENIX ISR PROJECT STARTS CONSTRUCTION IN ATHABASCA BASIN
snippet: Denison Mines Corp. (TSX: DML | NYSE: DNN) held a formal groundbreaking ceremony June 7 at its Wheeler River Phoenix project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — the first large-scale uranium mine to receive federal construction approval in Canada in more than two decades. Phoenix is also the first ISR (in-situ recovery) uranium project at commercial scale in Canada, avoiding the environmental footprint of open-pit or underground mining. With a February 2026 Final Investment Decision confirmed and all provincial and federal permits in hand, construction is expected to take roughly two years, targeting first uranium production in mid-2028.

headline: WALL STREET KEEPS RAISING MP MATERIALS PRICE TARGETS — BANKS NOW VIEW IT AS A RARE EARTH MANUFACTURING PLATFORM, NOT JUST A MINER
snippet: BMO Capital upgraded MP Materials (NYSE: MP) to Outperform, Goldman Sachs initiated with a Buy at $77, and Wedbush set an Outperform target at $90 — all after Q1 2026 revenue of $90 million crushed the $70 million consensus. The cluster of upgrades reflects a fundamental reframing: analysts no longer value MP as a mining company but as an integrated rare-earth manufacturing platform, as it scales Mountain Pass production alongside a new Northlake, Texas NdFeB magnet facility targeting 10,000 metric tonnes per year — the foundation for US rare-earth magnet supply independence by 2028.

headline: GOLDSEEK: JUNE IS GOLD'S WORST SEASONAL WINDOW — BUT 2026 SUMMER DOLDRUMS ARE THE MOST BULLISH ENTRY POINT IN YEARS
snippet: Adam Hamilton's seasonal analysis at GoldSeek argues gold has entered its annual summer doldrums — historically the weakest 6-8 week window, with most of the slump compressed into June and early July. But this year's setup is unusually bullish: after the jobs-shock selloff, gold has fallen to its least-overbought technical levels in years, setting up for the sequential autumn-winter-spring rally cycles that have historically followed summer lows. The implication for junior gold mining investors with a 6-12 month horizon: seasonal pressure through early July may be a positioning window, not an exit signal.

headline: KITCO: MINING M&A ENTERS NEW GROWTH PHASE — BUT INVESTORS NOW PUNISH MISSED GUIDANCE AND COMPLICATED PORTFOLIOS
snippet: Nicole Adshead-Bell (director, Cupel Advisory) tells Kitco that mining M&A has entered a genuine growth phase as rising metals prices give companies capital and strategic options — but the market is now harshly punishing complicated portfolios, missed guidance, and weak technical oversight far more than in prior cycles. Companies with operational track records command a meaningful 'execution premium' in their valuations. Recent examples: Pan American Silver's disciplined $146M Timmins Camp Phase 1 approval (June 1) and Allied Gold's ongoing Zijin acquisition, extended to a July 29, 2026 outside date as final West African regulatory approvals proceed.
